description: Return everything this server has recorded about a domain from earlier scans, without running a new one: current and past technologies with first-seen and last-seen dates, the latest email posture (MX provider, SPF and DMARC policy, DKIM selectors, high risks), and a dated change log (technologies added or removed, DMARC weakened, DKIM key lost, MX provider changed, score drops). Use it to spot a prospect that just adopted or dropped a tool, or to see how a domain's email security has moved over time. known=false means the domain has never been scanned here; run inspect_tech_stack or verify_email_infrastructure first. Cost: 1 credit.

changesLimit.description: Maximum number of recorded changes to return, newest first.

domain.description: Domain to inspect. Accepts a bare hostname ("example.com"), a URL ("https://www.example.com/pricing") or an email address ("jane@example.com"). Scheme, path, port and query are stripped; IDN names are accepted.

name: domain_history

creditsCharged.description: Prepaid credits this call itself charged: 0 for plan keys (they spend daily quota instead) and 0 for start_bulk_check, whose up-front charge is reported in job.creditsCharged and job.quotaUnitsCharged; creditsRemaining already reflects it.

change.description: What changed, e.g. tech_added, tech_removed, dmarc_policy, spf_policy, mx_provider, dkim_lost, risk_new, score_drop.

dmarcPolicy.description: reject | quarantine | none; unknown when a subdomain's own _dmarc lookup failed and only the organizational record answered; null when there is no record (dmarcFound false) or the record has no valid policy.

lookupsFailing.description: Components whose latest lookups failed. Their fields are the last known values while the failure is held, or the current (failed) reading once it was accepted as persistent (three scans over at least a day). A component also listed in unverified has no last known value.

score.description: Null until a scan in which every lookup answered or whose remaining failures were accepted as persistent (three scans over at least a day).

spfPolicy.description: fail | softfail | neutral | pass | none; unknown when an SPF redirect= target's lookup failed, so the terminal all policy could not be read. Read spfFound first: without a record this reads none.

unverified.description: Components not yet established: no lookup has answered them and their failure has not yet been accepted as persistent (three scans over at least a day); their fields come from a failed lookup, not the domain's real posture. An empty list therefore does not mean every component has answered: check lookupsFailing. Even once accepted, DMARC stays here while only the organizational fallback of a failed own _dmarc lookup has answered. SPF whose redirect= target has never answered leaves this list once the failure is accepted (spfPolicy reads unknown), so changes to the domain's own record are still reported, including its removal (an accepted failure of its own TXT lookup reads as one) and one that stops delegating to that target. While the record still delegates to it, the first scan in which the whole redirect= chain answers is a baseline, not a change, for the terminal policy and the findings that describe it, and the first such scan with spfLookups established is the include tree's baseline; until then, the first reading in which the target answered but a later hop's failure was accepted is a baseline too, and later such readings are compared with it. Each also re-baselines the score: no score_drop or score_rise for that scan or, when another lookup failed in it, for the next scan that rewrites the score.

known.description: False when this server has never scanned the domain; every other field is then empty.

title: Domain Change History
